text:
Predicates:
Animals(x) ::: x is an animal.
BredBack(x) ::: x is bred-back.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Premises:
∀x (BredBack(x) → Animals(x)) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
Animals(heckCattle) ∧ BredBack(heckCattle) ∧ Resemble(heckCattle, aurochs) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs.
Animals(heckCattle) ∧ Animals(aurochs) ::: Heck cattle are animals. Aurochs are animals.
∃x (Animals(x) ∧ Resemble(x, extinctAnimals)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
Extinct(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are extinct.
